decisions.diagnosis: Both directions read exactly 0 for seven days (Fri to Fri, stopping and resuming in working hours) on a path that normally carries 100-200 bikes a day; this could be a counter outage reporting zeros or a path closure for works, and with no nearby counter the data cannot tell them apart.
decisions.evidence: Daily N/S: 05-18 60/59, 05-19 14/17, 05-20..05-25 all 0/0 (TfNSW status warning), 05-26 9/40, 05-27 65/108; last counts 09:15 (N) and 10:30 (S) on 05-19, first again 12:45 (S) and 15:00 (N) on 05-26; no rain event or holiday known for that week.

decisions.diagnosis: Both directions cut out in the same slot (Fri 11:15) and came back together at Tue 07:45 with normal peak counts, which could be a counter outage or a short path closure; no neighbour is available to check whether bikes passed.
decisions.evidence: 02-26 11:00 slot 4/6 bikes, then exact 0 in both directions until 03-02 07:45 (5/1); 02-27..03-01 daily 0/0 with warning status, against surrounding weekend days of 114-136 N / 190-226 S.

decisions.diagnosis: Seven days of exact zeros in both directions coincide with the March 2021 NSW flood rain, so they may be real (a flooded or closed path by the Georges River) or a counter that stopped while waterlogged; the data do not settle it.
decisions.evidence: 03-18 14/29 and 03-19 13/24 (rain), 03-20..03-25 0/0 with warning status, resuming 03-26 ~11:00 with 37/67 and a 151/351 rebound Sunday 03-28; other very wet days here (2016-06-05, 2018-11-28) also read 0 or near 0.

decisions.diagnosis: TfNSW's site comment says MetroCount raised potential issues with this period, but the counts show no clear fault: the north/south split is lower than usual, as in the weeks just after it and in the 2019 winter.
decisions.evidence: Weekly S/N ratio 1.01-1.43 in the period vs 1.06-1.16 for 2021-08-16..09-20 and 0.75-1.4 in May-Aug 2019; totals follow the 2021 lockdown-winter level (about 60/80 per day); no zeros, duplicates or even-count runs.

summary: Site 112 has a single MC5720 piezo counter (154) with an almost unbroken 1-record-per-slot record from July 2011 to September 2026, a gap from October 2021 to August 2022, and no duplicate, doubled or spike faults; the March-Sunday peaks are a recurring organised ride, and the April 2020 surge is the COVID-era boom. The only questionable periods are three week-long runs of exact zeros in both directions (May 2017, Feb-Mar 2021, and March 2021 during the floods), recorded as uncertain because no neighbouring counter can show whether bikes passed, plus a low-confidence note on the July-August 2021 period flagged in TfNSW's site comment. With one counter at one site, no series definition is needed.
